mainEntity.name: How much does an Audi A3 Sportback e-tron 40 TFSI e engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: The cost to replace an Audi A3 Sportback e-tron 40 TFSI e engine typically ranges from £2,000 to £4,000 for a rebuilt unit, depending on whether you choose supply-only or supply & fit.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of engine disconnect clutch failure in an Audi A3 Sportback e-tron 40 TFSI e?

acceptedAnswer.text: Common symptoms include a "Drive System Fault" warning on the dashboard, the combustion engine failing to start or engage, and error codes like P288400 (Clutch Stuck Open).

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in an Audi A3 Sportback e-tron 40 TFSI e?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, if the vehicle is in good overall condition and valued above £8,000, a reconditioned or rebuilt engine is a cost-effective alternative to buying a new car.

mainEntity.name: How long does an Audi A3 Sportback e-tron 40 TFSI e engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A professional supply & fit service for the Audi A3 Sportback e-tron 40 TFSI e typically takes 1 to 2 days.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between the CUKB and DGEA engine codes in the Audi A3 Sportback e-tron 40 TFSI e?

acceptedAnswer.text: The CUKB is the 1.4L TFSI engine used in the 8V generation (2014-2020), while the DGEA is the updated 1.5L TFSI EVO engine used in the 8Y generation (2020-present).

problems.h4: Engine Disconnect Clutch Failure - Why the Audi A3 Sportback e-tron 40 TFSI e (CUKB/DGEA) Wears Prematurely
problems.affectedModels: Audi A3 Sportback e-tron 40 TFSI e (CUKB, DGEA, 2014-present)
problems.rootCause: The clutch that disconnects the combustion engine from the electric motor can stick open or fail to engage, triggering drive system faults and preventing the petrol engine from starting or assisting.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Diagnostic reset and clutch adaptation via ODIS
repairOptions.longevity: Temporary fix; only suitable if mechanical wear is minimal

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, upgraded clutch components, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: The right call when the hybrid drive system fault is persistent and mechanical

problems.vehicleValueCheck: - Vehicle worth under ~£5,000: repair or used engine typically makes more sense than a full rebuilt unit. - Vehicle worth ~£5,000-£8,000: evaluate both; reconditioned is viable if keeping the car 2+ years. - Vehicle worth ~£8,000-£15,000: reconditioned/rebuilt usually justifies the premium via warranty and reliability. - Vehicle worth £15,000+: replacement cost is typically small relative to vehicle value. A typical 8V Audi A3 Sportback e-tron 40 TFSI e (2014-2020) currently falls into the £5,000-£12,000 band, making a reconditioned replacement a financially viable option if you plan to keep the vehicle. Newer 8Y models (£15,000+) comfortably absorb the replacement cost.
problems.recommendation: If the issue is purely a software glitch or 12V battery drain, a diagnostic reset is the most cost-effective first step. However, if the engine disconnect clutch has mechanically failed or the high-voltage system is compromised, a rebuilt engine assembly from a specialist is the most reliable long-term solution.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt CUKB/DGEA Audi A3 Sportback e-tron 40 TFSI e engine prices

problems.h4: Water Pump & Coolant Leaks - Why the Audi A3 Sportback e-tron 40 TFSI e (EA211) Wears Prematurely
problems.affectedModels: Audi A3 Sportback e-tron 40 TFSI e (CUKB, DGEA, 2014-present)
problems.rootCause: The EA211 engine family is known for plastic thermostat housing and water pump failures, which can lead to coolant loss and potential overheating if ignored.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace pump, thermostat housing, and coolant flush
repairOptions.longevity: Highly recommended as a preventative or early-stage repair

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, upgraded components addressing the original failure point, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Necessary only if overheating has caused catastrophic head gasket or block damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: Given the £5,000-£15,000 value of most A3 e-tron models, a £400-£700 specialist water pump replacement is vastly preferable to a full engine swap, provided the engine has not already overheated.
problems.recommendation: Address coolant leaks immediately. A £500 water pump replacement is a minor expense compared to the £3,000+ cost of a full engine replacement caused by overheating. If the engine has already seized from coolant loss, a rebuilt unit is your only viable path forward.

items.question: What are the signs of engine disconnect clutch failure in an Audi A3 Sportback e-tron 40 TFSI e?
items.answer: Common symptoms include a "Drive System Fault" warning on the dashboard, the combustion engine failing to start or engage, and error codes like P288400 (Clutch Stuck Open).
keyPoints: The car may default to electric-only mode or refuse to drive.
A clicking or grinding noise may be heard from the bell housing.
Diagnostic scans will confirm hybrid system communication errors.

items.question: What is the difference between the CUKB and DGEA engine codes in the Audi A3 Sportback e-tron 40 TFSI e?
